Lessons.Title: Changing the Vertex
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: construct quadratic expressions for specified vertex positions by changing h and k, explain horizontal and vertical translations and preserve the effect of a on opening. Independent Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition U06:L17 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/6/17/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/6/17/index.html (CC BY 4.0). This source reverses the previous tasks: students start with desired vertices and design equations.

Original design requirement: create an upward-opening parabola with vertex(−1,5), scaled vertically by2 from y=x². One valid function is f(x)=2(x+1)²+5. It reaches minimum5 at x−1 and f(0)=7. Another target vertex(3,−2), same shape and opening, is g(x)=2(x−3)²−2, obtained by shifting the vertex4 right and7 down.

Graph g has zero values when2(x−3)²−2=0, so (x−3)²=1 and roots2 and4; vertex at(3,−2). At x0, g=2×9−2=16. Changes in h shift left/right, changes in k shift up/down; the outside factor a=2 maintains relative curvature.

Student task: given three desired vertices, write valid vertex-form functions with chosen a and justify signs; compare f and g at their vertices and one reflected pair; critique a formula using (x+3)² for vertex+3. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 for valid equation from a target vertex, accurate translations, graph features and reasoned sign choices.

KeyConcepts.Title: Horizontal and vertical translation
KeyConcepts.Definition: Changing h moves graph horizontally; changing k moves it vertically.

KeyConcepts.Title: Keep shape
KeyConcepts.Definition: Holding a fixed preserves opening and relative vertical stretch.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Compare same horizontal offsets from vertex.
KeyConcepts.Example: Both use a=2 and open upward.
